implementation_revision.semantics: WELL-16 recovery capability introduced in PR #228. WELL-17 changes shared Identity, Account and Token source bytes without changing recovery authority; the real primary-email-change/recovery PostgreSQL race in both commit orders is linked here and in identity.primary_email_change.json. File hashes bind inspected implementation bytes; this is not independent merge certification. WELL-20 extracts existing proof assertions into shared scenarios; original test names remain callable wrappers. Business semantics are unchanged. WELL-131 refreshes source evidence for shared files only; this capability lifecycle is unchanged. WELL-134 refreshes the shared browser-boundary source after global endpoint redaction, explicit legal dispatch, unknown-path denial and bounded parser-error handling. Domain registration/recovery ownership and durable lifecycle are unchanged. WELL-112 adds exact DEV-only guide dispatch in the shared browser boundary. Recovery controller dispatch and all owning recovery interfaces, guards and durable state remain unchanged. WELL-137 updates exact current Product and Decision lineage checks to v1.18.0 while retaining existing recovery content and approval boundaries. WELL-136 refreshes shared source references after independent semantic review; this mapped capability remains unchanged. WELL-153 changes TEST-only recovery restart diagnostics and proof; Identity and password-reset business semantics remain unchanged. WELL-153 coordinates registered TEST restart workers with P805 cleanup; no business lifecycle or Domain authority changed. WELL-153 now owns fixture admission before any global snapshot through safe scoped cleanup, restoration and release. VM-local quarantine retains exact synthetic targets across guardian failure; explicit reconciliation verifies registered workers and recorded OS process groups before retrying cleanup. No production Domain semantics changed. WELL-153 correlates each sequential TEST external-launch reservation. Proven pre-open validation or missing/non-executable launcher failure settles only its matching reservation; post-open uncertainty retains admission and reports unconfirmed cleanup. Production business behavior is unchanged. WELL-159 replaces the timed child sleep and mixed interruption/retry loop with an observed pre-commit checkpoint handshake, registered process-group termination, independent rollback assertions and a fresh-VM retry of the same case/operation. Fixed TEST-only transaction phases distinguish early failures; the 250ms public request cap and all Domain/business semantics are unchanged. PR271 failure diagnosis distinguishes a neutral public acknowledgement from committed fixture state. Initial unverified fixture setup and ordinary child resume use at most three same-operation requests with durable state reads; the child retains the historical ordinary :requested result. Interruption-enabled requests remain single-attempt. Explicit TEST rollback and bounded-exhaustion cases prove retry and fail-closed setup; fixed restart diagnostics survive aggregate exception redaction. WELL-159 independently proves real 250ms lease expiry at transaction entry, after Account lock and after uncommitted Token/MessageIntent work. The worker reports its own PostgreSQL XID; a separate parent connection observes aborted before release, then the old lease must raise DBConnection.ConnectionError. Full Case/Account and zero partial effects are checked before explicit fresh-BEAM retry, which must commit one version/proof/intent. Initial fixture requests now own isolated Scenario worker checkouts so a bounded request cannot disconnect the fixture owner. Shared atomics are TEST fault counters only. Failed cleaned-up requests log identifier-free durable observations and still fail the cut/retry assertion; skipped-cut control must have committed a valid request. WELL-157 advances current Product-route verification to v1.19.0 through the exact v1.18.0 predecessor; the existing Phase-8 content meanings and delivery boundaries remain unchanged. WELL-161 evaluates the accumulated TEST port output on the READY transition and after later data messages. It checks the existing absolute deadline and output cap before accepting the complete interruption handshake, and sends stdin only after verified process-group ownership and READY. WELL-148 moves the verified-channel resume test onto an isolated unboxed recovery request worker and shares the existing restart fixture request mechanism. The fixture guardian registers the worker before it acquires the checkout, and the test waits for worker cleanup before reading durable state. WELL-156 refreshes locators in shared source files. The new ordinary primary-email-change routes and context do not change this capability contract. The WELL-156 correction refreshes shared source references. Verified recovery containment also terminalizes an active Phase-9 primary-email change in its existing transaction where applicable. WELL-146 refreshes the shared EmailChangeScenarios source locator after the held-notice proof correction. WELL-143 extends shared TEST creation ownership to MessageIntent and Session identifiers. Magic request observations and full-row Token/Session fingerprints exclude independent fixtures while retaining unexpected owned consequences. Maintenance proof separately checks foreign expired rows are restored after actual global maintenance rollback. P815 retains reset operation and account identifiers before JTI-based delivery. Production lifecycle and fixed proof inventory are unchanged; this evidence does not clear the unresolved P809 canonical failure. WELL-143 reconciles the retained reset proof with the WELL-148 lease. A registered worker uses its own unboxed connection and observation scope under the single lease. The proof verifies the foreign reset remains valid and unchanged after the race. The stale-reset race uses the existing registered Recovery fixture request worker and verifies the committed operation before proceeding. WELL-164 adds fixed TEST diagnostics for restart child transaction failures. WELL-166 strengthens TEST-only request replay and completion guards with durable proof linkage and adds a separate same-VM request cut. It preserves fresh-BEAM and lease-expiry evidence and changes no runtime lifecycle or owner interface. WELL-168 gives Recovery signing-key unavailability its own source-guard outcome so Communications can retry the same obligation. WELL-167 adds TEST-only ownership-proxy exit and first-query-failure observation on the fresh hosted request. The second deliverable changes the actual request transaction budget to 350 ms and retains the 500 ms public response floor. The expiry and cut controls use the owning Recovery budget. WELL-175 verifies the exact current Product v1.20.0 pair before reading the historical approval chain. The routed Phase-9 applicability packet records four existing locale versions. The runtime still consumes the P8-15 packet, with no normal-entry Phase-9 path. WELL-183 adds the bounded ordinary Phase-9 entry and preserves the separate historical P8-15 transport. Identity persists the entry context on each RecoveryCase. Communications persists the corresponding render schema on each intent and revalidates Identity and the routed WELL-175 evidence before invocation. The browser renders only WELL-184 copy in the ordinary context and directs a completed claimant to the existing password-session route for fresh authentication. The WELL-183 review follow-up proves Phase-9 versus Phase-9 requests and both Phase-9 versus P8-15 commit orders on distinct PostgreSQL backends. The Master Gate follow-up proves historical operator approval and completion for the same synthetic target, then tests the separate Phase-9 approval and completion denials. WELL-189 refreshes shared source references. The mapped behavior is unchanged. WELL-210 refreshes shared source references after semantic review: the controller test and the approved Recovery packet path now point at v0.3.0. The approved wording and loader checks are unchanged. The mapped behavior is unchanged.

request_flow.summary: Neutral request locks Account and creates/reuses one durable case. Missing verified channel remains case-only held at zero assurance.
Identity issues the existing Token and Communications obligation transactionally. Exact current approved content binds when available; otherwise the obligation remains held.

Communications revalidates source and content, commits attempt admission and invocation fence, then invokes only the deterministic TEST provider outside any transaction. Unknown submission requires reconciliation.
Passive link retrieval renders an explicit CSRF-protected confirmation form. Explicit POST consumes proof; a separate guarded password POST completes ordinary recovery.
Completion atomically establishes credential/revocation consequences, receipt, security notice and E2 work. Manual exceptions first require independent E1. Delivery and Audit cannot execute recovery.

Ordinary DEV/TEST entry selects WELL-183 on the server, requires current exact browser Content and admits only synthetic example.test Accounts. The scoped P8-15 fixture selects historical entry when ordinary entry is off.

After explicit confirmation, Identity requires current matching case, locale and proof. A hold renders the unavailable page. Successful completion clears the browser session and uses the existing /login and /session/protected dispatch for a new password authentication. Ordinary completion calls Identity.complete_recovery/5 with signed proof, replacement password, operation UUID, exact locale and server-selected context.

security_invariants.summary: Required and satisfied assurance never decrease within a case. The unsupported permanent Account-wide recovery floor was removed; new cases re-evaluate current Account risk.
Anonymous or unverified requests create no Account hold, credential effect or Session/Device revocation. Zero-factor manual completion is denied.
Terminal cases never reopen and never automatically release a separately justified Account hold. MFA, email verification, Privacy and entitlement authority are not created by recovery.

Bearer values are serialized transiently from fixed existing Token claims, never ordinary intent fields, Audit, telemetry or job arguments. Exact email bytes are immutable; support contact is a non-secret render input.
Production and external delivery remain disabled. Current development content approval does not prove support-mailbox operability or provider permission.

The ordinary context cannot consume historical proof or enter the historical manual approval/completion path. The executor checks the context against the durable case and rechecks both locale bindings before using a queued proof or notice.

concurrency.summary: Account row locks precede recovery case and Token locks; account-wide Session/Device invalidation locks linked authentication Tokens by JTI before sorted Session and Device rows. Support actor/reviewer Accounts lock in stable order before scoped authority revalidation.
Unique active Account case/request/completion/proof indexes prevent parallel weaker authority. Genuine PostgreSQL races cover proof/completion, login/reset and fixture email commits.
The actual Identity.apply_primary_email_change/1 interface and existing recovery completion serialize in genuine PostgreSQL transactions; WELL-17 proves both commit orders and stale-write denial.
The Communications intent lock, one-active-attempt index and invocation marker serialize provider admission; uncertain calls cannot be retried as safe absence.

The proof observes the contender blocked by the winning Account transaction and verifies its return after release. Two ordinary requests and both mixed-context commit orders retain one case and one proof obligation in the winning context. Correct proof acceptance and its identical retry advance the case once. Cross-context proof and wrong-locale Phase-9 proof leave the case and Token untouched.

idempotency_retry.summary: Request retries reuse the current case and cannot reduce assurance. Exact acceptance/completion IDs return durable receipts without repeating credential or notice/evidence effects.

Communications causal identity rejects conflicting source retries. An unbound held recovery obligation can select current eligible exact content once under the intent lock; a previously bound snapshot cannot be replaced. Provider evidence is independently authenticated and replay controlled.
Manual review and completion re-read current scopes, step-up, Account hold and recorded independent approval after E1; stale authority cannot reuse prior admission as permission.

Passive confirmation renders the existing untrusted case UUID as a stable retry key only. A fresh browser explicitly POSTs again to recover the same accepted receipt without another case transition. GET never queries Identity or establishes proof; forged signatures cannot use the key to advance recovery.

An ordinary completion retry requires the original signed proof and operation ID plus the still-current committed Account binding and replacement password. It returns the receipt without a new credential, Session, device revocation, Audit or notice write.

failure_recovery.summary: Returned errors/crash before source commit roll back Token, case, credentials and required consequences together. Existing P8-04 cut points prove interrupted transactions.
E1 survives later failed source effects; durable E2 obligations and notices reconstruct independently of one Oban job or process.
Fresh BEAM processes reconstruct case/proof/completion receipts from PostgreSQL. Consumed proof metadata is retained for durable completion and notice provenance.

Content absence preserves held obligations. Restored eligibility permits a one-time initial content binding through the private Communications action without replaying Identity completion. Current source, content, rendering and provider guards still run before admission and invocation. Revoked proof closes without submission; crash after invocation remains ambiguous until authenticated evidence.

An unavailable signing key keeps an otherwise current proof intent held with no new admission. A reconciliation-required intent continues waiting for provider evidence. Restoring the same key permits the existing intent to pass the current guards again before proof expiry. A revoked or mismatched proof still closes without submission.

The TEST guardian admits one correlated outstanding launch. It records the Port before OS identity lookup and completes the matching reservation after transfer. Proven no-child failures settle that reservation; an interrupted launch without recorded identity remains quarantined and rejects later launches. An interrupted transfer with a recorded target can reconcile only after existing worker, Port and OS-group checks pass.

TEST restart proof accepts a cut only after complete checkpoint markers and confirmed cleanup of the registered process group. It reads durable rollback before retrying the same operation/case in a fresh VM. An interruption request has one attempt: early failure, missing checkpoint, deadline or uncertain cleanup remains failed proof. Ordinary fixture setup/resume may explicitly repeat the same public request at most three times, checking durable state each time; exhaustion is not success. The child reports a rejected await_proof transition separately from fixed database failure categories observed on its own checkout. A closed lease establishes that the connection became unusable. Attribution to a deadline or another test requires separate evidence.

TEST real-deadline proof is independent of final-checkpoint child termination. It requires PostgreSQL to report the exact worker transaction aborted and the old connection to be unusable; elapsed time or a neutral public acknowledgement is insufficient. Manual retry is driven by the TEST controller and does not prove automatic browser retry. Initial fixture requests use isolated registered worker leases and acknowledged cleanup.

Unavailable message Content leaves a durable held obligation. Withdrawal after admission closes the attempt before invocation. Reopening confirmation can recover a current proof-acceptance receipt and a separate BEAM can recover the completion receipt.

cases: Explicit proof and completion, assurance, anonymous restrictions, terminal/replay, hold causation, rollback and expiry.

A valid verified-channel resume reaches proof-pending with a Token and held MessageIntent inside its transaction. An injected wait before COMMIT expires the configured request lease. The fixture owner retains its PostgreSQL backend and observes the exact XID aborted, the held Case and Account unchanged, and no recovery Token, MessageIntent or hold obligation. The original operation then advances the same Case once with one linked Token and held intent.

Verified issuance and request replay preserve one case with exactly one linked recovery Token and account_recovery MessageIntent. Early completion with a valid unconsumed proof leaves the case, Account and pending effects unchanged, then the same completion identity succeeds once after explicit acceptance.
tests.proves: Real owner actions and PostgreSQL constraints.
tests.limits: Synthetic fixtures with a controlled pre-COMMIT lease expiry. The historical hosted stack was in COMMIT, so the original transaction outcome and cause of the delay are unknown. The neutral acknowledgement is not a commit receipt.

cases: Current scoped step-up, distinct reviewer/actor, zero-factor denial, E1 before effect, failed source and hold-release independence.

The same current P8-15 operator grants, sessions and synthetic target permit historical approval and completion. Phase-9 approval is denied before Audit admission. A test-only current review reaches the separate Phase-9 completion guard, which denies before admission, outcome evidence, notice or credential change.
tests.proves: Proof-backed higher-assurance positive and unsupported-factor negative paths.
tests.limits: Does not implement future lost-all-factor verification.

cases: Separate PostgreSQL transactions, duplicate proof/completion, stale login/reset/email fixture, hold escalation, crash and fresh BEAM restart.

Observed pre-commit child termination, unchanged entire RecoveryCase and Account plus zero tokens/intents before same-operation retry; one final proof/intent, preserved zero assurance and strict missing-checkpoint denial with cleanup.

First neutral setup transaction rolls back, then valid same-operation fixture commits; three failed setup attempts fail closed; an observed child pre-commit rollback retries with one final proof/intent. Interruption requests cannot use these ordinary retries to claim an unobserved cut.

Real pre-checkpoint lease expiry at transaction entry, Account lock and after uncommitted Token/Intent creation. Bound XID observed aborted independently, expired worker lease confirmed, unchanged complete Case/Account and0effects before manual fresh-BEAM retry with exactly1version/proof/intent. Valid commit without expiry is rejected. A real initial lease timeout must leave fixture owner usable. Missing-cut control must have committed valid proof work before denial.
stale-reset recovery race preserves a valid independent owner's reset proof

A separate connection confirms the parked same-VM worker's PostgreSQL backend holds its exact in-progress XID before authorizing the registered cut. It observes that XID aborted after the monitored worker exits and before the earliest possible configured lease expiry, with unchanged Account and case and no partial effects. A new unboxed worker resumes the original operation and commits one correctly linked proof and intent. The negative control waits for real lease expiry and rejects the already-aborted XID before authorizing a cut.

On GitHub-hosted runners or the explicitly selected Blacksmith 2-vCPU runner, calibration checks a per-job database marker and the same committed case and operation in both processes before inducing expiry or explicit check-in. Successful and timing-only resumes provide comparison controls.
Opt-in hosted budget characterization records stage and public durations for first and repeated requests on separate fixtures, with independent durable-effect checks.

WELL-183 observes real lock contention and committed returns for two Phase-9 requests and both mixed-context orders. With a now-verified channel, conflicting same-operation and distinct-operation locale/context retries cannot resume the original held case. The eligible retry advances it once with one bound Token and intent.
A wrong-context claimant cannot replay the committed proof-acceptance operation.
tests.proves: Owner-side serialization and restart from durable truth. Reset prerequisite lookup uses its operation and account identifiers while a valid independent reset proof remains unchanged and usable.
tests.limits: This recovery-specific legacy test still uses a fixture email competitor; the real owner-interface integration is covered by the WELL-17 test below. The same-VM cut does not exercise child boot, Port acknowledgment or process-group handling. The existing fresh-BEAM positive and live negative controls cover those boundaries separately.

cases: Actual apply-versus-recovery PostgreSQL transactions in both commit orders.
tests.proves: Recovery and canonical-email apply serialize through their owning Identity interfaces; stale competing writes cannot overwrite the committed winner.
tests.limits: The test uses the isolated local PostgreSQL test database and does not exercise a deployed production service.

cases: Exact EN/AF proof and notice, provider acceptance/unknown/rejection, withdrawal at invocation fence, three crash cuts and competing executors.
Missing-content completion notice and proof recover after current eligibility restoration; one-time binding, private policies and revoked-source denial.
Temporary signing-key outage and restoration on the same unexpired content-bound intent, revoked proof during outage, and accepted or unknown provider evidence during outage.
tests.proves: Actual Communications executor, DeliveryAttempt fencing and deterministic P8-04 provider non-authority. A separate PostgreSQL checkout verifies the held and terminal dispositions and attempt counts. The fixture observes zero provider calls during outage and one across restoration and replay.
tests.limits: No external email, mailbox reachability, production or provider permission.

cases: Read-only exact source guard and completion-notice authority beyond proof expiry, revocation and later password reset.
tests.proves: Immutable notice source survives later mutable credential authority.
tests.limits: A source guard alone cannot admit a provider.

cases: Missing content keeps durable immutable obligations held without attempts.
tests.proves: Must-not-lose source handoff and conflicting retry denial.

cases: Four exact versions, unknown locales, altered bindings, withdrawn packet, corrupted approvals/authority, paired locale and symlink rejection.
Current v1.18 routing accepts approved content and changed v1.17 predecessor fails closed.
tests.proves: Current pinned approval and immutable bytes fail closed.
tests.limits: Owner provenance comes from WELL-110; this reader grants no sender authority.

cases: Scanner GET/HEAD, localized forms, actual CSRF-protected confirmation/password replacement/fresh sign-in, non-enumeration and telemetry.
Fresh browser reopens the delivered link after acceptance, explicitly recovers the same durable receipt without case advancement, then completes; a forged signature with the same form key is denied.
tests.proves: Real Phoenix transport calls owning Identity and Communications boundaries.
tests.limits: Development switch only; no production exposure or claimant factor invented.

cases: E2 obligations, manual E1-linked outcomes, rollback, evidence minimisation and restart.
tests.proves: Audit evidence does not execute or authorize Identity recovery.
tests.limits: Central evidence is derived from owner source outcomes.

cases: Safe bounded child status and marker classification, startup failure, output overflow, deadlines, cancellation, and process-group cleanup.
Complete checkpoint handshake permits registered-child termination; incomplete final line cannot authorize a cut. Returned phase diagnostics discard arbitrary output.

A single write coalesces READY and all checkpoint lines before a silent child. An incomplete buffered line must await its newline, and a missing newline cannot authorize interruption. Observations include confirmed cleanup, no live child and no leaked port messages.
The parser keeps allow-listed transition and database failure markers and discards arbitrary child output.
tests.proves: TEST-only subprocess outcomes and bounded cleanup under exercised Linux process conditions.
tests.limits: Does not reconstruct the lost historical child status or certify production recovery. The deterministic reproducer establishes the buffer defect. The chunk boundaries of the failed hosted attempts were not captured.

cases: Competing admission and rejection before any global environment snapshot; ownership retained during cleanup.
Real external child surviving worker death retains Account, RecoveryCase and recovery intent, denies new fixtures and rejects unsafe reconciliation.
Guardian death preserves the exact target; verified process-group absence permits scoped cleanup and restoration; stale reconciliation cannot release another fixture.
Proven no-child launch failure settles safely; stale settlement and overlapping reservation are rejected; successful sequential launches preserve all recorded targets.
A real post-open interruption in a separate TEST BEAM reports harness failure and unconfirmed cleanup, denies the next launch and retains quarantine after the exact child has stopped.
tests.proves: TEST fixture ownership, exact-target quarantine and actual database cleanup after independently observed external termination. Correlated sequential launch reservation settlement and truthful post-open diagnostics.
tests.limits: VM-local coordination and controlled Linux process groups; no claim to reconstruct the lost historical failure or certify production Recovery.

cases: Real Chromium EN and AF request, controlled proof delivery, passive retrieval, explicit POST, credential replacement, replay denial and fresh sign-in.
tests.proves: Exact approved bilingual copy, keyboard focus, responsive layout, reduced motion, revoked device trust and a durable completion notice.
tests.limits: Loopback server, repository synthetic fixture and TEST-only delivery adapter. No external provider or mailbox proof.

safe_extensions.summary: Maintain the existing owning Ash interfaces and Account-first current-authority guards when adding approved factors. A new claimant-verification method belongs to its separately approved workstream.

A future operational provider must independently establish approved support operability, sender/provider authority and protected delivery; never enable a production adapter through test configuration.

reuse.summary: Recovery uses existing password strategy hashing/guarded replacement, Session/Device owner actions, Identity Token, scoped privilege and Audit/Communications boundaries.
Browser composition, tokens and primary button follow existing authentication forms; shared labels and identical password-result copy are reused.

prohibited_shortcuts.summary: No second RecoveryProof Resource, raw Repo/Ecto.Multi business write API, workflow engine, additional Repo, Redis or process-authoritative cache.
Provider delivery, Audit admission, staff roles, UI claims and queued jobs never prove claimant identity or release Account holds.
Do not implement WELL-17 email change or new MFA/passkey methods here; recovery cannot verify or change canonical email.

proof_limitations: This descriptive map is subordinate to current routed authority and live Plane. Schema/hash validation is not semantic or independent merge review.

Provider evidence uses the existing deterministic TEST adapter and synthetic Accounts only. No external email was sent; support mailbox operation and external sender/provider permission are not certified.

WELL-20 reuses the existing primary-email owner action and both PostgreSQL commit-order scenarios for recovery/email-change integration. Production deployment and cross-region failure behavior remain outside this proof.

WELL-111 accepts proof-backed manual positive proof and zero-factor negative proof for Phase 8. Successful lost-all-factor recovery is unimplemented and remains a pre-release obligation under WELL-115; privileged hardening remains WELL-65.
Historical PR #217, PR #228 and Markdown handoffs remain historical evidence. The current WELL-20 candidate requires its own exact-head proof, CI and independent review.

WELL-112 source-reference refresh records the reconciled implementation, not a full-suite or integration pass. Current-base Content eligibility failures remain recorded under WELL-138 and WELL-136; canonical/deep, OCR, exact-head CI and independent certification remain separate obligations.

WELL-136 verification corrected only the P815 reset-versus-recovery fixture lookup to its own Account. The strengthened case creates an unrelated reset proof through Identity and asserts that Token remains unchanged after contention. Deterministic RED failed at the previous global-purpose lookup; GREEN passed all 13 recovery-concurrency tests with seed 441709 and four schedulers. No recovery business API or lifecycle was changed and no retained shared records were deleted. Full gate results remain separately required.

WELL-153 historically used a 400ms checkpoint sleep to observe a 250ms lease timeout. WELL-159 now observes parent-directed child termination after the checkpoint and independently checks rollback; connection_lost is not fabricated. Neither correction establishes the lost historical seed38448 cause or PR270 attempt1 seed243046 cause.

WELL-153 fixture ownership and retained targets are local to the running TEST BEAM. They survive guardian failure, not termination of the whole VM. External evidence is limited to recorded Linux process groups from the controlled restart launcher. Missing launch identity or uncertain process state remains fail-closed; reconciliation has no assertion-based or force-release override. This is not deployed recovery certification.

WELL-159 original-seed full local execution at PR270 head55537186 passed993 tests; normal-resource focused seeds243046 and253534 passed35 each. A deliberately saturated two-core run with two CPU workers reproduced interruption_not_proven with transaction_entered/transaction_error and no checkpoint, and failed17/35 overall. This demonstrates a resource-sensitive failure signature, not the cause of the historical hosted run. Local Ubuntu26.04.1 and existing exclusive TEST allocation do not reproduce the exact historical hosted image or fresh CI database.
